project_title: The Pigeon Poop That Heard the Big Bang

scenes.headline: THE PIGEON POOP THAT HEARD THE BIG BANG
scenes.caption: In 1964, two scientists accidentally heard the birth of our entire universe. But for an entire year... they were convinced it was just warm pigeon shit.

scenes.headline: THE 50-FOOT ALUMINUM EAR
scenes.caption: Atop Crawford Hill in New Jersey sat the Holmdel Horn Antenna—an 18-ton aluminum giant built to bounce signals off giant orbiting NASA balloons.

scenes.headline: TWO PHYSICISTS AT BELL LABS
scenes.caption: Their names were Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson. With the satellite project completed, they took over the horn for pure radio astronomy.

scenes.headline: TUNED TO 4,080 MEGAHERTZ
scenes.caption: They chilled their receiver with liquid helium down to four Kelvin and tuned in to 4,080 megahertz, pointing into the quiet halo of the Milky Way.

scenes.headline: AN UNEXPLAINED 3.5 KELVIN HUM
scenes.caption: The strip-chart recorder registered an extra 3.5 Kelvin of steady, unyielding static. One hundred times stronger than any expected cosmic signal.

scenes.headline: RULE 1: IT IS ALWAYS OUR FAULT
scenes.caption: In physics, you never claim a breakthrough first. You assume your equipment is broken and begin hunting down earthly interference.

scenes.headline: ELIMINATING THE SUSPECTS
scenes.caption: They checked New York City broadcasts, military coastal radars, and even Starfish Prime nuclear fallout. One by one, every suspect was ruled out.

scenes.headline: IT WAS COMING FROM EVERYWHERE
scenes.caption: They rotated the giant horn across 360 degrees. The hum was completely isotropic. Identical in day, night, winter, and summer.

scenes.headline: CRAWLING INTO THE HORN THROAT
scenes.caption: Desperate, Penzias and Wilson put on coveralls and climbed physically inside the aluminum horn to inspect every millimeter of the waveguide.

scenes.headline: WHITE DIELECTRIC MATERIAL
scenes.caption: Deep in the narrow throat, they found two roosting pigeons. And coating the aluminum walls was a layer of warm white dielectric material.

scenes.headline: THE HOMING PIGEONS RETURN
scenes.caption: They trapped the pigeons in a box and mailed them sixty miles away. But being homing pigeons, they flew right back into the horn.

scenes.headline: THE BROOM SCRUB: 3.5K PERSISTS
scenes.caption: The birds were permanently evicted, and the horn was scrubbed with brooms and alcohol. They turned on the receiver: the 3.5 Kelvin hum remained.

scenes.headline: THE PRINCETON THEORISTS
scenes.caption: Thirty miles away at Princeton University, astrophysicist Robert Dicke and Jim Peebles were calculating the death rattle of the early cosmos.

scenes.headline: THE PRIMORDIAL FIREBALL
scenes.caption: If the Big Bang was true, the searing fireball of creation must have cooled over billions of years into a faint, ubiquitous bath of microwaves.

scenes.headline: HUNTING THE MICROWAVE GHOST
scenes.caption: Dicke's team was actively constructing a radiometer on the roof of the Princeton physics building, hoping to catch this cosmic glow.

scenes.headline: WELL BOYS, WE HAVE BEEN SCOOPED
scenes.caption: When Penzias called Dicke to ask about antenna noise, Dicke listened in silence, hung up the phone, and told his colleagues: Boys, we have been scooped.

scenes.headline: THE JULY 1965 PACT
scenes.caption: In July 1965, the two teams published companion papers in the Astrophysical Journal, jointly resolving the greatest mystery in cosmology.

scenes.headline: TWO PAPERS, ONE TRUTH
scenes.caption: Penzias and Wilson reported the raw numbers with pure understatement. Dicke and Peebles explained what it meant: the echo of the Big Bang.

scenes.headline: THE STEADY STATE IS DEAD
scenes.caption: The discovery dealt a fatal blow to the Steady State model of the universe. The cosmos had a definite beginning in time.

scenes.headline: THE 1978 NOBEL PRIZE
scenes.caption: In 1978, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson received the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the Cosmic Microwave Background.

scenes.headline: RECOMBINATION: 380,000 YEARS
scenes.caption: Today satellites like COBE, WMAP, and Planck have mapped this relic radiation across the entire sky with breathtaking fidelity.

scenes.headline: THE SATELLITE LEGACY
scenes.caption: Tiny temperature fluctuations in this glow reveal the primordial seeds that condensed into every galaxy, star, and planet in existence.

scenes.headline: THE STATIC ON YOUR OLD TV
scenes.caption: If you ever turned an old cathode-ray TV to an empty channel, roughly one percent of that dancing snow was radiation from the Big Bang itself.

scenes.headline: THE UNIVERSE WAS WHISPERING
scenes.caption: All it took was two stubborn physicists, an 18-ton aluminum horn, and a refusal to let the pigeons win.
